html:
On Easter Monday, 24 April 1916, about 1,200 Irish rebels seized the General Post Office and other buildings in Dublin and proclaimed an Irish Republic. They surrendered after six days.

The Irish Republican Brotherhood planned the rising while Britain was fighting the First World War, and Patrick Pearse read the proclamation. British troops shelled the centre of Dublin. About 500 people died, more than half of them civilians.

At first most Dubliners did not support the rebels. But the British executed sixteen leaders, including Pearse and James Connolly, and arrested thousands. Opinion swung. In 1918 Sinn Féin, linked in the public mind with the rising, won most Irish seats and declared independence, which led to the War of Independence. W. B. Yeats wrote of it: a terrible beauty is born. See Ireland.
sum: On Easter Monday, 24 April 1916, about 1,200 Irish rebels seized the General Post Office and other buildings in Dublin and proclaimed an Irish Republic. They surrendered after six days.
